title: What competence management system must an EU railway undertaking or infrastructure manager have?
description: Directive (EU) 2016/798 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 section 4.2: the competence management system, training programs and refresher rules.
shortAnswer: Directive (EU) 2016/798 requires every railway undertaking and infrastructure manager to run a safety management system that includes training programs and systems to keep staff competence maintained. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762, which applies in all Member States from 31 October 2020, sets the detail in section 4.2: a competence management system covering competence identification, selection, initial and ongoing training, periodic assessment, and recorded, regularly audited training programs with back to work arrangements.
keyTakeaways: Article 9(3)(f) of Directive (EU) 2016/798 makes training programs and systems to maintain staff competence a basic element of every railway safety management system.
Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 sets SMS requirements in Annex I for railway undertakings and Annex II for infrastructure managers; both contain the same section 4.2 on competence.
Section 4.2.1 lists six minimum elements, from identifying competencies including non-technical behaviors to periodic assessment of competence and fitness.

Section 4.2.2 requires training programs to reflect individual needs, cover normal, degraded and emergency conditions, set appropriate refresher frequency, keep records for all staff, and be reviewed and audited.

A single safety certificate is renewed at intervals not exceeding 5 years and an infrastructure manager's safety authorization is valid for 5 years, and both are assessed and supervised against these requirements.
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States with a rail system; Cyprus and Malta exempt while they have none)
regulator: European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) and national safety authorities, under Directive (EU) 2016/798 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762
appliesTo: Railway undertakings holding or applying for a single safety certificate
Infrastructure managers holding or applying for a safety authorization
Staff with a role that affects safety, including management
Contractors performing safety-related tasks for railway undertakings or infrastructure managers

sections.heading: Where does the competence requirement come from?

blocks.text: The requirement starts in the Railway Safety Directive and is detailed in a common safety method. Article 9(1) of [Directive (EU) 2016/798](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02016L0798-20201023) on railway safety requires infrastructure managers and railway undertakings to establish safety management systems, and Article 9(3)(f) lists as a basic element "the provision of programmes for the training of staff and systems to ensure that the staff's competence is maintained and that tasks are carried out accordingly, including arrangements with regard to physical and psychological fitness".

Article 9(2) adds that the SMS must show "a clear commitment to consistently apply human factors knowledge and methods" and must promote a culture of mutual trust, confidence and learning. Member States had to transpose the relevant articles by 16 June 2019, with an optional extension that ran no later than 31 October 2020 (Article 33).

[Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02018R0762-20200616) establishes the common safety methods (CSMs) on SMS requirements. Article 3 applies Annex I to railway undertakings and Article 4 applies Annex II to infrastructure managers, for assessing applications and for supervision. As amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/782, it applies in all Member States from 31 October 2020, and it repealed Regulations (EU) No 1158/2010 and No 1169/2010 with effect from 31 October 2025.

sections.heading: What does section 4.2 of the CSM on SMS require?

blocks.text: Section 4.2.1 requires a competence management system ensuring that "staff having a role that affects safety are competent in the safety-related tasks for which they are responsible". It must include at least six elements:

items: identification of the competencies, including knowledge, skills, non-technical behaviors and attitudes, required for safety-related tasks;
selection principles, covering basic educational level and the psychological and physical fitness required;
initial training, experience and qualification;
ongoing training and periodic update of existing competencies;
periodic assessment of competence and checks of psychological and physical fitness to ensure qualifications and skills are maintained over time;
specific training in the relevant parts of the safety management system needed to deliver safety-related tasks.

blocks.text: Section 4.2.2 then requires a training program for staff performing safety-related tasks that ensures:

items: delivery according to the identified competency requirements and the individual needs of the staff;
where applicable, that staff can operate under all operating conditions: normal, degraded and emergency;
training duration and refresher frequency that are appropriate for the training objectives;
records kept for all staff, under the SMS control of documented information in section 4.5.3;
regular review and audit of the program through internal auditing (section 6.2), with changes made when necessary through management of change (section 5.4).

blocks.text: Section 4.2.3 requires back to work arrangements for staff following accidents or incidents or long absences, including additional training where a need is identified.

sections.heading: Which other SMS clauses depend on competence?

blocks.text: Competence is referenced throughout the SMS requirements, not only in section 4.2. An assessor reviewing a single safety certificate application will follow these cross references.

items: **Roles and delegation (2.3.2):** staff with delegated responsibilities for safety-related tasks must have the authority, competence and resources to perform them without being adversely affected by other business functions.
**Resources (4.1):** the organization must provide the resources, including competent staff, for establishing and improving the SMS.

**Human and organizational factors (4.6.1):** a systematic approach using recognized methods, addressing risks from the design and use of equipment, tasks, working conditions and organizational arrangements, taking account of human capabilities and limitations.

**Operational control (5.1.6):** staff must comply with training and work instructions, receive specific training ahead of anticipated changes affecting operations or task assignment, and adequate measures must follow accidents and incidents.
**Contractors (5.3):** contracts must specify the level of competence required to deliver the contracted tasks.
**Emergency management (5.5):** the organization must describe how training requirements for emergencies have been identified.
**Internal auditing (6.2):** auditors must be identified and selected as competent.

blocks.text: Entities in charge of maintenance have a parallel requirement. Annex III to Directive (EU) 2016/798 lists competence management, defined as "a structured approach to ensure that employees have the competences required in order to achieve the organisation's objectives safely, effectively and efficiently in all circumstances", among the criteria for ECM certification.

Competence management is assessed at certification and then checked during supervision. Under Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2016/798, the single safety certificate provides evidence that the railway undertaking "has established its safety management system and that it is able to operate safely in the intended area of operation"; it is issued by ERA or, for operations in one Member State, optionally by the national safety authority.

items: A single safety certificate must be renewed on application at intervals not exceeding 5 years (Article 10(13)).
An infrastructure manager's safety authorization is valid for 5 years and may be renewed (Article 12(2)).

Every infrastructure manager and railway undertaking must submit an annual safety report to the national safety authority before 31 May, including the results of internal safety auditing (Article 9(6)).

blocks.text: The European Union Agency for Railways states on its [safety management system page](https://www.era.europa.eu/domains/safety-management/safety-management-system_en) that the SMS "is not a paper-based system specifically developed for demonstrating compliance with the regulatory framework". For competence, that means assessors look for evidence that the system works in practice: competence profiles in use, assessments carried out, and records that show refresher training actually happened.

sections.heading: What does the CSM leave to the organization?

blocks.text: The CSM sets outcomes, not hours or intervals. Section 4.2.2(c) only requires refresher frequency to be "appropriate for the training objectives", so each organization must justify its own intervals, ideally from risk assessment, incident data and assessment results.

Role specific rules come from elsewhere. Train drivers have prescriptive licensing, certification and periodic check requirements under Directive 2007/59/EC, covered on the [EU train driver licensing and training](/regulations/eu-train-driver-licensing-and-training) page. Annex II to Directive (EU) 2016/798 also allows Member States to notify national safety rules on staff executing safety-critical tasks, including selection, medical fitness, vocational training and certification, where not yet covered by a TSI.

blocks.title: Practical consequence
blocks.text: For roles without prescriptive EU rules, such as signallers, track workers, train dispatchers or maintenance staff, the competence management system is the main legal basis for training. The organization's own competence profiles, refresher intervals and assessment methods become the standard it is audited against.

sections.heading: Are these requirements current as at November 2026?

blocks.text: Yes. As at November 2026, the latest consolidated text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 on EUR-Lex is dated 16 June 2020, incorporating Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/782, and the latest consolidated text of Directive (EU) 2016/798 is dated 23 October 2020. The repeal of Regulations (EU) No 1158/2010 and No 1169/2010 took effect on 31 October 2025, so older safety management guidance that cites those regulations is out of date.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry builds the competence profiles required by section 4.2.1(a) as structured frameworks of knowledge, skills and non-technical behaviors, with assessment points for normal, degraded and emergency conditions. Training content and assessments trace back to those profiles, giving assessors a direct line from each SMS requirement to the evidence.

faqs.q: Does the CSM on SMS set a refresher training interval for railway staff?
faqs.a: No. Section 4.2.2(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 requires the duration of training and the frequency of refresher training to be appropriate for the training objectives. Each railway undertaking or infrastructure manager must set and justify its own intervals, except where role specific rules such as Directive 2007/59/EC for train drivers apply.

faqs.q: Do contractors fall under the competence management system?
faqs.a: Yes, indirectly. Article 9(4) of Directive (EU) 2016/798 requires the SMS to control risks including the use of contractors, and the CSM requires contracts to specify the level of competence needed for the contracted tasks. The railway undertaking or infrastructure manager should verify contractor competence against its own profiles.

faqs.q: Are the requirements different for railway undertakings and infrastructure managers?
faqs.a: The competence requirements are the same. Annex I of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 applies to railway undertakings and Annex II to infrastructure managers, and both contain the same section 4.2 on competence. Other parts of the annexes differ to reflect each organization's activities.

faqs.q: Must non-technical skills be part of rail competence management?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 4.2.1(a) requires identification of the competencies required for safety-related tasks, explicitly including knowledge, skills, non-technical behaviors and attitudes. Section 4.6 separately requires a systematic approach to human and organizational factors, so communication, situational awareness and similar skills belong in competence profiles.
